title: Fusilli al Ferretto
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Fusilli al Ferretto are Calabria's hand-rolled corkscrew pasta, twisted around a thin wire, traditionally paired with the region's fiery, spreadable nduja sausage.
longDesc: The 'ferretto' — a thin metal rod, traditionally a knitting needle — is used to roll and coil each individual piece of pasta into its distinctive spiral, a slow, meditative process still practiced by hand in many Calabrian households.
ingredients: 400 g (3⅓ cups) durum wheat semolina flour, plus more for dusting
60 g (¾ cup) grated Pecorino, plus more for serving
equipment: Thin metal rod or wooden skewer
steps: Combine the semolina flour, water, and salt into a firm dough. Knead for 10 minutes until smooth. Rest, covered, for 30 minutes.
Pinch off small pieces of dough and roll into thin ropes. Wrap each rope around a thin metal rod or skewer, rolling it under your palm to create a tight spiral, then slide it off.
Repeat with all the dough, laying the shaped fusilli on a floured tray.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook briefly, then add the crumbled nduja, letting it melt into the oil, about 2 minutes.
Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until thickened.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the fusilli for 5–7 minutes until tender.
Drain and toss with the sauce and Pecorino.
chefTips: Nduja is quite spicy and salty — taste the sauce before adding extra salt.
The hand-rolling technique takes practice; work steadily rather than rushing for the most even spirals.
A clean, thin wooden skewer works well if a traditional ferretto isn't available.
commonMistakes: Rolling the dough too thick, resulting in a heavy, dense pasta rather than a delicate spiral.
Adding nduja over too high heat, which can cause it to separate rather than melt smoothly.
Over-salting before tasting, given nduja's inherent saltiness.
servedWith: A robust Calabrian red wine such as Cirò
storage: The sauce keeps refrigerated for up to 3 days; uncooked fusilli can be dried for room-temperature storage.
reheating: Reheat the sauce gently, then toss with freshly cooked fusilli.
healthBenefits: A good source of protein from the pasta and nduja.
Capsaicin from the spicy nduja may provide a metabolic boost.
culturalNote: Fusilli al ferretto is a defining shape of Calabrian cuisine, and nduja — a spreadable, spicy pork sausage from the town of Spilinga — has become one of the region's most internationally recognized culinary exports.
